 # snapshot toolchain

-snapshots of a directory and rotate old ones out.

+    snapshot.sh      makes one archive, replicates it, prints one manifest record
     prune.sh         reads manifest records, rotates old archives out
     run-backup.sh    runs snapshot.sh, feeds its manifest to prune.sh
 
 ## Usage
 
-    ./run-backup.sh --label nightly --config /etc/backup.conf
+    ./run-backup.sh --label nightly --config /etc/backup.conf [--force]
 
 `run-backup.sh` is the only entry point cron needs. `snapshot.sh` and
 `prune.sh` are usable on their own, which is why each one loads its own
 config and validates its own inputs instead of trusting the caller.
 
+`--force` (or `BACKUP_FORCE=1`) downgrades the pre-flight free-space check
+from fatal to a warning. Use it when you know the archive filesystem has
+room that `df` cannot see, e.g. because a large archive is about to rotate

+
 ## Config file
 
 `load_config` reads `KEY=VALUE` lines and exports only keys beginning with
 `BACKUP_`; anything else is logged and skipped so a typo in the config
 cannot clobber `PATH`. Recognised keys:

     BACKUP_ARCHIVE_DIR   where archives are written       (required)

-    <epoch>\t<bytes>\t<archive-path>

+v1 records had no label column; the label had to be recovered from the

+written. `run-backup.sh` treats that as success and skips rotation, so a
+host that has not produced any data yet cannot rotate its last good

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # common.sh -- helpers shared by snapshot.sh, prune.sh and run-backup.sh.
 # This file is sourced, never executed.
 
-BACKUP_LIB_VERSION="1.4.0"
+BACKUP_LIB_VERSION="1.5.0"
 
 # Archives kept per label when BACKUP_KEEP is not set.
 DEFAULT_KEEP=5
 
+# The umask moved out of snapshot.sh and up here on purpose. Every script in
+# the toolchain now writes something derived from the source tree -- prune.sh
+# lists it, run-backup.sh spools a manifest through /tmp -- and those two used
+# to run with whatever umask cron happened to hand them.
+umask 077
+
 log() {
   printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$*" >&2
 }
 
 die() {
   log "FATAL: $*"
   exit 1
 }
 
 require_cmd() {
   local cmd
   for cmd in "$@"; do
     command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $cmd"
   done
 }
 
 # epoch_of <path> -- mtime in seconds since the epoch.
 epoch_of() {
   local path="$1"
   case "$(uname -s)" in
     Darwin|*BSD) stat -f %m "$path" ;;
     *)           stat -c %Y "$path" ;;
   esac
 }
 
 # load_config <path> -- read KEY=VALUE lines and export the BACKUP_* ones.
 # Anything else is reported and skipped, so a stray line in an operator's
 # config file cannot overwrite PATH, HOME or IFS.
 load_config() {
   local path="$1" key value
   [ -r "$path" ] || die "config not readable: $path"
   while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
     case "$key" in
       ''|\#*)   continue ;;
       BACKUP_*) ;;
       *)        log "ignoring non-BACKUP key in config: $key"; continue ;;
     esac
     export "$key=$value"
   done < "$path"
 }
+
+# make_stage -- create the scratch directory for one run and print its path.
+# Staging used to be snapshot.sh's business alone, but replication needs
+# somewhere to hold a finished-but-not-yet-published archive too.
+make_stage() {
+  local stage
+  stage="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/snapshot.XXXXXX")" ||
+    die "could not create a staging directory under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
+  printf '%s\n' "$stage"
+}
+
+# check_free_space <dir> <need_kb> <force> -- refuse to start a run that would
+# probably fill the archive filesystem. <force> carries the caller's --force /
+# BACKUP_FORCE setting; when it is on, a shortfall is logged and not fatal.
+check_free_space() {
+  local dir="$1" need_kb="$2" force="$3" avail_kb
+  avail_kb="$(df -Pk "$dir" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }')"
+  case "$avail_kb" in
+    ''|*[!0-9]*) die "could not read free space for $dir" ;;
+  esac
+
+  if [ "$avail_kb" -ge "$need_kb" ]; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+
+  if [ "$force" ]; then
+    log "only ${avail_kb}KB free in $dir, wanted ${need_kb}KB -- continuing anyway"
+    return 0
+  fi
+
+  die "not enough space in $dir: ${avail_kb}KB free, need ${need_kb}KB (--force overrides)"
+}
+
+# replicate <archive> -- stream one archive to the off-host replica named by
+# BACKUP_REMOTE (user@host), into BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR. The far side writes with
+# cat rather than scp so that a connection dropped mid-stream cannot leave a
+# partially transferred file sitting under the archive's final name.
+replicate() {
+  local archive="$1" name
+  name="$(basename "$archive")"
+  require_cmd ssh
+  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$BACKUP_REMOTE" \
+    "mkdir -p '$BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR' && cat > '$BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR/$name'" \
+    <"$archive" || die "replication of $name to $BACKUP_REMOTE failed"
+  log "replicated $name to $BACKUP_REMOTE:$BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR"
+}

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # prune.sh -- rotate old archives out.
 #
 # Reads snapshot.sh manifest records on stdin:
 #     <epoch>\t<bytes>\t<archive-path>
 # and for every label mentioned there keeps the newest BACKUP_KEEP archives
 # in that archive directory, deleting the rest.
 
 set -euo pipefail
 
 HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
 # shellcheck source=lib/common.sh
 . "$HERE/lib/common.sh"
 
 KEEP="${BACKUP_KEEP:-$DEFAULT_KEEP}"
 case "$KEEP" in
   ''|*[!0-9]*) die "BACKUP_KEEP must be a non-negative integer, got: $KEEP" ;;
 esac
 [ "$KEEP" -ge 1 ] || die "BACKUP_KEEP must be at least 1"
 
 # list_archives <dir> <label> -- archive paths for one label, newest first.
+#
+# This used to be a `for file in "$dir/$label"-*.tar.gz` glob. On the two file
+# servers the archive directory now holds tens of thousands of entries and the
+# expanded glob was overrunning the command line, so the same set is collected
+# with find instead: -maxdepth 1 keeps it as non-recursive as the glob was, and
+# -print0 keeps names with spaces intact. Ordering is unchanged.
 list_archives() {
   local dir="$1" label="$2" file
-  for file in "$dir/$label"-*.tar.gz; do
-    [ -f "$file" ] || continue
+  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
     printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(epoch_of "$file")" "$file"
-  done | sort -rn | cut -f2-
+  done < <(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$label-*.tar.gz" -print0) |
+    sort -rn | cut -f2-
 }
 
 # prune_label <dir> <label> <keep>
 prune_label() {
   local dir="$1" label="$2" keep="$3" file
   local idx=0
   while IFS= read -r file; do
     idx=$((idx + 1))
     [ "$idx" -gt "$keep" ] || continue
     rm -f "$file"
     log "pruned $file"
   done < <(list_archives "$dir" "$label")
   log "label=$label kept up to $keep of $idx archives in $dir"
 }
 
 seen=""
 while IFS=$'\t' read -r epoch bytes path; do
   [ -n "${path:-}" ] || continue
   log "manifest record: epoch=$epoch bytes=$bytes archive=$path"
   if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
     log "manifest points at a missing archive, skipping: $path"
     continue
   fi
   dir="$(dirname "$path")"
   base="$(basename "$path")"
   label="${base%%-*}"
   # One run can emit several records for the same label; rotate once.
   case "$seen" in
     *"|$dir/$label|"*) continue ;;
   esac
   seen="$seen|$dir/$label|"
   prune_label "$dir" "$label" "$KEEP"
 done

# snapshot toolchain

Three small scripts plus a shared library that take periodic compressed
snapshots of a directory, replicate them off-host, and rotate old ones out.

    lib/common.sh    logging, config loading, staging, space check, replication
    snapshot.sh      makes one archive, replicates it, prints one manifest record
    prune.sh         reads manifest records, rotates old archives out
    run-backup.sh    runs snapshot.sh, feeds its manifest to prune.sh

## Usage

    ./run-backup.sh --label nightly --config /etc/backup.conf [--force]

`run-backup.sh` is the only entry point cron needs. `snapshot.sh` and
`prune.sh` are usable on their own, which is why each one loads its own
config and validates its own inputs instead of trusting the caller.

`--force` (or `BACKUP_FORCE=1`) downgrades the pre-flight free-space check
from fatal to a warning. Use it when you know the archive filesystem has
room that `df` cannot see, e.g. because a large archive is about to rotate
out on the same run.

## Config file

`load_config` reads `KEY=VALUE` lines and exports only keys beginning with
`BACKUP_`; anything else is logged and skipped so a typo in the config
cannot clobber `PATH`. Recognised keys:

    BACKUP_SOURCE_DIR    directory to snapshot            (required)
    BACKUP_ARCHIVE_DIR   where archives are written       (required)
    BACKUP_KEEP          archives kept per label          (default 5)
    BACKUP_REMOTE        user@host of the replica         (optional)
    BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR    directory on the replica         (required with the above)
    BACKUP_FORCE         1 to pre-set --force             (optional)

## Manifest format (v2)

`snapshot.sh` writes exactly one tab-separated record to stdout:

    <label>\t<epoch>\t<bytes>\t<archive-path>

v1 records had no label column; the label had to be recovered from the
archive filename, which stopped working the moment a label contained a `-`.

`prune.sh` consumes those records on stdin. It uses the record only to
learn which directory and which label to rotate; the rotation decision is
made from what is actually on disk, so a stale manifest can never delete
an archive that a later run created.

## Exit status

`snapshot.sh` exits 3 when the source tree is empty and nothing was
written. `run-backup.sh` treats that as success and skips rotation, so a
host that has not produced any data yet cannot rotate its last good
archive out from under itself.

## Archive naming

    <archive-dir>/<label>-<UTC timestamp>.tar.gz

item.text:
The new manifest format disables rotation, and the default force handling defeats the disk-space guard. Failure cleanup and remote publication also introduce data-integrity, disk-exhaustion, and permissions risks.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Update prune.sh for the v2 manifest — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.bPHO3C/snapshot.sh:94-94
  Every successful snapshot now emits four fields, but `prune.sh` still reads only `epoch bytes path`; Bash assigns `bytes<TAB>archive` to `path`, so its file check fails and every run silently skips rotation. Parse the label field in `prune.sh` and use it instead of deriving the label up to the first `-`.

- [P1] Treat the default force value as disabled — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.bPHO3C/lib/common.sh:81-83
  When free space is insufficient on an ordinary invocation, `snapshot.sh` passes the literal `0`, but `[ "$force" ]` is true for every nonempty string. The preflight therefore always downgrades a shortage to a warning and proceeds toward filling the filesystem; compare explicitly with `1` or use an empty false value.
